paras: Lygisaurus parrhasius, also known commonly as the fire-tailed litter-skink and the fire-tailed rainbow-skink, is a species of lizard in the subfamily Eugongylinae of the family Scincidae. The species is native to northwestern Australia.
The specific name, parrhasius, commemorates ancient Greek artist Parrhasius.

The head of Lygisaurus parrhasius is coppery brown. The body is black with five white stripes, which are vertebral, dorsolateral, and midlateral. The tail is bright red. Adults usually have a snout-to-vent length (SVL) of about 3.3 cm (1.3 in).
Lygisaurus parrhasius is found in Queensland, Australia.
The preferred natural habitat of Lygisaurus parrhasius is rocky areas.
